blocks.content: The demography chapter is unusually important for DNH&DD because Dadra & Nagar Haveli has one of the highest proportions of Scheduled Tribe population of any district-level unit in India — a statistic that appears constantly in comparative exam questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Scheduled Tribes constitute 8.6% of India's total population according to the 2011 Census.
Bhil is recognized as the largest tribal community in India, followed by the Gond and Santhal tribes.
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution includes 22 officially recognized languages.
India's overall literacy rate stands at 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.

cells: ≈ 5.86 lakh (585,764) — Dadra & Nagar Haveli ≈ 3.43 lakh; Daman & Diu ≈ 2.43 lakh
≈ 50% of the district's population — one of the highest ST proportions of any district in India outside the North-East and Fifth/Sixth Schedule areas
≈ 774 females per 1,000 males (one of India's most skewed, largely due to male migrant industrial labour inflow)
Varies sharply by district; Daman & Diu's urban districts post notably higher literacy than rural, tribal Dadra & Nagar Haveli
Large in-migration of industrial workers to Dadra & Nagar Haveli from across India, drawn by manufacturing employment

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Dadra & Nagar Haveli's ~50% Scheduled Tribe population share and its heavily male-skewed sex ratio (driven by migrant factory labour) are two of the most repeated demographic one-liners for this UT.

cells: The most numerous tribal community of Dadra & Nagar Haveli; traditionally agriculturalist, with the Dhodia language (an Indo-Aryan/Gujarati-related dialect) as mother tongue for many
A major tribal group, also found across the border in Maharashtra and Gujarat's Valsad-Dangs belt; traditionally forest-dependent and agricultural

Well known nationally for the distinctive Warli painting tradition (white pigment on mud-red or ochre backgrounds, depicting daily/ritual life) — a major cultural export from this tribal belt (shared with neighbouring Maharashtra's Warli heartland)

Smaller tribal groups found in scattered pockets across the territory, each with distinct traditional occupations (Kathodi historically associated with catechu/khair extraction, Kolis with fishing in coastal pockets)

rows: Surpassed Gonds as the largest tribal population
Highest absolute ST population in India
Over 94% of state population belongs to STs
Spoken by ~43.6% of the total population

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Warli painting — one of India's most recognisable tribal art forms, using simple white-on-earth-tone geometric figures — is strongly associated with the Varli/Warli tribe of this region (and adjoining Maharashtra), a frequently tested culture-cum-tribe crossover fact.

items: Gujarati and Marathi are the two most widely spoken languages given the territory's position between Gujarat and Maharashtra, alongside Hindi as a link language.
Tribal languages/dialects — Dhodia, Varli, Kokna, Bhilodi/Bhili — remain in everyday use within their respective communities, especially in rural Dadra & Nagar Haveli.

In Daman and Diu, Portuguese-influenced Konkani and Gujarati are both spoken, with some older residents retaining familiarity with Portuguese from the colonial era, especially in Diu's older Catholic community.
Madhya Pradesh accounts for the highest absolute population of Scheduled Tribes in India, while Mizoram has the highest percentage share among states.
The 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act added four languages—Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali—to the 8th Schedule.
There are 75 recognized Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India, with Odisha having the largest number of PVTGs.

Hinduism is the majority religion across all three districts; Dadra & Nagar Haveli's population is predominantly tribal-Hindu (with syncretic tribal religious practices blending local deity worship with mainstream Hindu festivals).

Daman and Diu retain small but historically significant Roman Catholic Christian communities, a direct legacy of over four centuries of Portuguese rule and missionary activity — visible today in the region's numerous Portuguese-era churches (see Chapter 7).
Islam and smaller religious minorities are also present, particularly in the urbanised trading and fishing communities of Daman and Diu.
Combined UT population ≈ 5.86 lakh (2011); Dadra & Nagar Haveli ≈3.43 lakh, Daman & Diu ≈2.43 lakh.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli: ≈50% Scheduled Tribe population — Dhodia (largest), Kokna/Kokni, Varli, plus smaller groups (Koli, Kathodi, Naika, Dubla).
Varli/Warli tribe — famous for Warli painting, a widely recognised Indian tribal art form.
Gujarati & Marathi dominant languages; tribal dialects (Dhodia, Varli, Kokna) remain in local use.
Daman & Diu retain a historic Roman Catholic Christian minority from Portuguese colonial times.
